title: Kanye 'Ye' West Possibly To Be Sued By George Floyd's Family
htmlContent:
George Floyd a 46-year-old black man, who was murdered in the U.S. city of Minneapolis by Derek Chauvin, a 44-year-old white police officer. Who is now serving a 252 month sentence. Floyd family is allegedly pursuing a lawsuit against Kanye West.

His family claims that the billionaire rapper who goes by the name Ye, made false accusations about Floyd’s death. According to a medical examiner the autopsy ruled that police officers' restraint of Floyd and compression of his neck were the primary causes of death.

Kanye recent appearance on Drink Champs Hip Hop Podcast. He questioned the cause of Floyd's death, suggesting it was because of fentanyl use that was also found in his system and not by Derek Chauvin who kneeled on his neck for 9 1/2 minutes.

Chauvin's knee "wasn't even on his neck like that," Ye said. He also said, his claims were supported by a documentary by conservative commentator Candace Owens. Candace who’s also being considered by Floyds family, to file legal proceedings against as well. In the club “Aayan Fix My Life” hosted by AayanX and co-host Wack100 on the clubhouse app.

A steamy controversial conversation struck over the topic by many Ye fans and Pro George Floyd supporters. A post on Akademiks IG account regarding the topic according to Wack100 was flagged and removed. West’s remarks about Floyd come amid backlash for recent social media posts by West that were criticized as anti-Semetic!

Wack 100 was able to get REVOLT TV to take down the whole Drink Champs Interview with Ye down.

Speaking of West, he recently purchased Parler, the Conservatives' preferred alternative social media platform.

Parler's parent company announced the deal on Monday morning, saying West had pulled off “a groundbreaking move into the free speech media space and will never have to fear being removed from social media again.”

West added, “In a world where conservative opinions are considered controversial, we have to make sure we have the right to freely express ourselves."
